clue.text: Colourful design in second Mediterranean vessel

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
a saic is a ketch-like sailing vessel of the eastern Mediterranean

explanation.surface: A bright pattern painted on a Mediterranean boat in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: A SAIC is a crossword-favourite boat from the Levant; MO is the informal 'half a mo', a second.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture built from small coloured tiles is a classic decorative pattern, so it is a colourful design.

clue.text: Unintelligible work, one somewhat lacking in appeal

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
a means one

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the appeal word is removed

parts.note: quite means somewhat, fairly
it is slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A dull, incomprehensible piece of writing that is rather short of charm.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex appeal comes from 'the It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Prose that is impenetrable or hard to understand is figuratively not see-through.

clue.text: Ideal place almost in a group for George

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch

indicators.note: almost means the ideal place loses its final letter

parts.note: Utopia is an imaginary perfect society

explanation.surface: Nearly paradise among a party for someone called George.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George' is pilots' slang for the automatic flying system, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Airline crews nicknamed the automatic flight-control device George, so the name is a slang synonym.

clue.text: Tons crews replaced in elevated position at sea

indicators.note: placed again in a new order, so the letters of tons and crews are rearranged

explanation.surface: Masses of sailors moved to a high post aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the lookout platform high on a ship's mast, a raised post at sea.

clue.text: Worker ludicrously busy round English church

indicators.note: the frantic word goes round the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: manic means frantically, absurdly busy

explanation.surface: A worker rushing frantically around an English church.
explanation.definitionFit: A garage or machine repairer is a skilled manual tradesman, a kind of worker.

clue.text: Old lady supported by formidable dog

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so it comes after

parts.note: ma is a mother, an old lady in slang
stiff means hard, severe, as in stiff competition

explanation.surface: An elderly woman propped up by a fearsome hound.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large, powerful breed of guard dog, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Skill shown by hundred, a large number

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a raft of things is a large number of them

explanation.surface: Expertise shown by a hundred, a large crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft means dexterity or expertise in making things, a synonym of skill.

clue.text: Patterned fabric that's limitless in part of church

indicators.note: without limits means both outer letters of the fabric are removed

parts.note: paisley is a fabric with a teardrop pattern

explanation.surface: A fabric with an endless pattern in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The passage between rows of pews is a section of a church building.

clue.text: Small measure in section of hospital is soon to happen

parts.note: one millimetre, written 1mm, read as IMM
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A tiny dose given in a hospital ward is about to be administered.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 is read as the letter I, so 1mm gives IMM.
explanation.definitionFit: Something about to occur at any moment is impending, close at hand.

clue.text: Wary scout I redirected in tour of a university

indicators.note: a tour goes round something, so the shuffled letters wrap around the rest
sent in a new direction, so the letters of scout and I are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scout, redirected, makes a careful tour of a university campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redirected' scrambles SCOUT I to CTIOUS, and 'tour of' puts A and U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wary is careful about danger, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Appropriate turkey, bird held back

parts.note: a turkey is a fool or flop, as is an ass

indicators.note: held back suggests turned round, so the bird's name runs backwards

parts.note: the emu is the large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: Someone helps themselves to a turkey while a second bird is kept back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' is the verb, to take over, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate power or a role is to take it on, which is one sense of the verb in the answer.

clue.text: Furore created by odd drug dealer (not half)

parts.note: rum is an old-fashioned word for odd or strange

indicators.note: only half of the dealer's word is kept, its first three letters

parts.note: a pusher sells illegal drugs

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over a strange drug dealer who is only half there.
explanation.walkthrough: '(not half)' looks like slang emphasis, but it halves PUSHER to PUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy commotion or uproar is a furore, the same sense as a din or row.

clue.text: At last, plan to guard explosive

indicators.note: guarding means surrounding protectively, so the plan word encloses the explosive

parts.note: to intend is to plan
HE stands for high explosive

explanation.surface: A scheme to keep watch over a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means finally, after everything, which is what at last says.

clue.text: Tone cut in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing means as heard, the word is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: to hew is to chop or cut

explanation.surface: A tone of voice cut short at a court hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tone is a shade or tint of colour.

clue.text: File to handle differently in current circumstances

indicators.note: the letters of file, to and handle are arranged in a different way

explanation.surface: Advice to deal with a document in another way given how things now stand.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the state of affairs as it stands, the present situation.

clue.text: Hard ancient judges to preside over attendants

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
old means ancient
a court is a body of judges

explanation.surface: Severe old judges presiding over their court staff.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to talk to a gathered audience of admirers as a monarch would.

clue.text: Sadly only spare figure without expertise

indicators.note: sadly suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of only and spare are scrambled

explanation.surface: Unfortunately only a spare person lacking any specialist knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-professional with no specialist training is an individual without expertise.

clue.text: Drink taken by daughter amid outstanding praise

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the drink and daughter go inside

parts.note: ace means excellent, outstanding

indicators.note: the drink is taken by the daughter, who follows it

parts.note: cola is a fizzy drink

explanation.surface: A girl drinking a soft drink gets excellent acclaim.
explanation.definitionFit: An award or expression of admiration is a tribute, an act of praise.

clue.text: Friend behind city still in joyful mode

indicators.note: the friend comes after, behind, the other pieces

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
static means still, unmoving
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A companion stays motionless behind a city, happily.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the City of London's postal district, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with ecstasy means doing it in a delighted, joyful manner, an adverb like the phrase.

clue.text: American's behind passageway screens

indicators.note: screening means concealing, so the letters are hidden inside the passageway word

explanation.surface: A US rear end hidden by screens in a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: In US slang this word means the backside, a person's rear.

clue.text: Sweet stuff bordered by fancy lace

indicators.note: bordered means edged around, so the shuffled lace wraps the cramming word
fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters of lace are rearranged

parts.note: to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: Something sweet framed in decorative lace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet stuff' reads as one noun phrase, but 'stuff' is the verb, to cram; 'fancy' rearranges the lace letters to CAEL.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a chewy toffee-like confection, so a sweet in the British sense of a piece of candy.

clue.text: Changeable fellow facing predicament losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the predicament word drops its first letter

parts.note: being in a pickle means being in a predicament

explanation.surface: A changeable man facing a tricky situation loses his head.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose loyalties shift often is inconstant, the same as changeable.

clue.text: Lines penned by website contributor, expert on public views

indicators.note: penned means enclosed as in a pen, so the contributor word holds the lines

parts.note: someone who posts on a forum is a poster
L is short for line; LL is lines

explanation.surface: Lines written by someone posting online who claims to know public opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who conducts opinion surveys measures and interprets what the public thinks.

clue.text: Indefinite sun in Cornish resort

indicators.note: the sun letter goes inside the resort name

parts.note: Looe is a small fishing and seaside town in Cornwall
S is short for sun, as on old calendars for Sunday

explanation.surface: Vague sunshine at a Cornish seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: LOOE is a seaside town in Cornwall, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A vague or imprecise translation or arrangement is not exact, so not definite.

clue.text: What one might see after summer holiday dance

parts.words: What one might see after summer holiday
parts.note: after a summer break the brown skin fades away, the tan may go

parts.words: What one might see after summer holiday
parts.note: after a summer break the brown skin fades away, the tan may go

explanation.surface: A riddle about what happens to your colour after a summer break.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words: the suntan goes, fading after the holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a passionate Argentine ballroom dance, an example of a dance.

clue.text: Distinction retained in sacred itinerary

indicators.note: the letters are kept inside the run of sacred itinerary

explanation.surface: An honour kept within a holy travel plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A university pass at a high grade is graded credit or distinction, so the two are comparable marks of merit.

clue.text: Crimson strand

definitions.meaning: to leave someone stuck on a desert island or in isolation

explanation.surface: A red colour and a verb for abandonment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a brownish crimson shade, and also means to leave someone stranded somewhere.

clue.text: Incomplete dessert, otherwise termed a Greek dish

indicators.note: incomplete means the dessert loses its last letter

parts.note: a mousse is a light whipped dessert
AKA, also known as, means otherwise termed

explanation.surface: An unfinished pudding, also called a Greek dish.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a baked Greek dish of aubergine, minced meat and white sauce, a specific example.

clue.text: Information given on European game in stock source?

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
pool is the cue game played on a table

explanation.surface: Details provided about a European game in a stock exchange source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' means bloodline or lineage, not shares; the question mark flags the twist.
explanation.definitionFit: The total stock of inherited genetic variation in a population is where its lineage comes from.

clue.text: Sensitive proposal

definitions.meaning: sore and painful to the touch
a formal offer, as in a bid for a contract

explanation.surface: Two meanings: a sore spot and a bid.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruise can be sore to touch, and a firm puts in a formal bid or offer for a contract.
